4. Date of commencement of : 15.03.2024  recording of evidence 5. Date of closing of evidence : 15.03.2024 6. Offences Complained are : U/sec.498(A), 323, 504,

7. Opinion of the Judge : Charges not proved  JUDGMENT

This case is registered on the basis of the charge sheet submitted by the ACP, Yalahanka Sub Division against the accused U/sec.498(A), 323, 504, 506 of IPC & sec.4 of DP Act, &
u/s.3(1)(r),(s),(z) of the SC/ST POA) Act, 1989.
2. The case of the prosecution is that the accused No.1 married complainant on 10.02.2012 at Dharmasthala Manjunatha Swamy Temple, inter-caste marriage.
On 13.02.2012, they further registered their marriage in the office of Sub-Registrar, Hebbal.
Later accused had left the victim in her maternal house.
The accused used to visit there, but, he did not took the victim alongwith him to the matrimonial house.
3. On 12.12.2015 when the victim requested accused No.1 to take to his house, acccused No.1 refused the same.
On 24.02.2016 the Kodigehalli police did not took the complaint of the complainant.
As the IO refused to take up the complaint the complainant was forced to file the PCR on 13.06.2017 before this court PCR No.31/2017 has been made reference of the same on 13.01.2018
Crime has been registered in Cr. No.176/2018 by the Jurisdictional IO.
4. Complainant was forced to lodge the complaint as she was abused, assaulted, demanded dowry.
She has been harassed by the Accused No.2 even though married Accused No.1 she was not allowing her into the house.
Further, the Accused No.2 and Accused No.1 demanded dowry.
In fact the victim belonging to Madiga caste is not entitled to eat or touch the food that was cooked by accused.
In the matrimonial house she was threatened that she has to face dire consequences and she has been driven out of the matrimonial house.
Accordingly, the complaint before the jurisdictional police.
On the basis of the complaint IO took up investigation and filed charge sheet.

On going through the charge sheet framed by my Predecessor in office, the same has been recasted on 26.7.2023.
5.
At trial, the prosecution got examined PW-1 and got exhibited Ex.P.1 to 5.

The statement of the accused persons u/sec 313 of Cr.P.C recorded, read over and explained to the accused persons in vernacular language and the accused persons, denied all the incriminating evidence and they did not choose to lead defence evidence.

6. On hearing both side the following points would arise for the determination of this Court are as follows;
Kodigehalli Ps vs A1 Venugopal Singh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169624525/
2 POINTS 1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 12.12.2015 police have made compromise and on 20.4.2016 accused did not take C.W.1 to his house after his marriage, when asked, on 22.4.2016 Kodigehalli police again called, he made house in Yelahanka Upanagara,
accused No.2 being the in-law of the C.W.1 informed accused No.1 not to have food in her house and subjected her to mental and physical cruelty by demanding dowry and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 498(A) r/w.34 of IPC?

3) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on aforesaid date, time and place, the accused persons in prosecution of their common intention abused C.W.1 with filthy language as "
   

 
,

 "
and intentionally insulted and thereby gave provocation to her intending that such provocation will cause the said CW1 to break the public peace and thereby committed the offence punishable u/s.504 r/w 34 of IPC within the cognizance of this Court?
4) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused persons in prosecution of their common intention the accused No.1 abused the C.W.1, accused No.2 attempted to snatch the mangalya chain of C.W.1 and has criminally intimidated by threatening the CW1 with injury to her person with intent to cause alarm to her and thereby committed the offence Punishable under Section 506 of IPC?
5) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention have demanded the CW1 to bring more dowry and thereby committed the offence punishable u/sec.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
6) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the afore said date, time and place, the accused persons are not being the members of SC/ST, knowing very well that CW1 belongs to SC/ST have intentionally insulted with intent to humiliate them in a place within the public view and thereby committed offence punishable u/s 3(1)(r) of SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
7) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused persons not being the members of SC/ST have abused CW1 being the members of Sc/ST by taking the name of their caste in a place within public view and thereby committed offence punishable u/sec 3(1)(r) of SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
8) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused persons not being the members of SC/ST even after knowing that she belongs to Kodigehalli Ps vs A1 Venugopal Singh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169624525/
3 schedule caste told her to leave the house and assaulted her in a place within public view and thereby committed offence punishable u/sec 3(1)(z) of SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
9) What order?
7. My findings to the above points are as follows;
Point No.1 : In the Negative Point No.2 : In the Negative Point No.3 : In the Negative Point No.4 : In the Negative Point No.5 : In the Negative Point No.6 : In the Negative Point No.7 : In the Negative Point No.8 : In the Negative Point No.9 : As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 8. Point Nos.1 to 4: All these Points are taken up together for discussion as they are interwoven.

sentences.text:
The prosecution to prove the alleged offence punishable u/s.498A, 323, 504, 506 R/W 34 of IPC,
basically relies on the evidence of the P.W.1 who has deposed that she married the accused No.1 as per the rituals.
This witness deposes she is belonging to Adi Karnataka caste and accused were belonging to Rajputs.

She did went to Kodigehalli police station to lodge the complaint but they did not take the same, as such she was forced to lodge private complaint PCR which got marked as Ex.P.1.
9.
The complainant deposes she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 since it is too long and she was being hurt at the time of giving complaint.
This witness admits her signature on Ex.P.2 the spot Mahazar and she identified Ex.P.3.
This witness deposes she does not remember why and when she had signed the documents.

This witness deposes about police visiting the house No.87, 6 th Main,
7th cross, Balaji Layout, Kodigehalli.
This witness deposes she cannot recollect what are the contents of the same as it is of more than 10 years she cannot remember the same.
This witness has been treated as hostile.
This witness denies the suggestions made by Learned SPP.
This witness denies that she has been demanded dowry, harassing for not giving dowry and she has been threatened with dire consequences if the demands of accused Nos.1 and 2 are not made.
This witness specifically admits she has been compromised with her husband.
This witness denies only due to threat and abuse made by accused Nos.1 and 2, she had made complaint.
This witness admits M.C.No.6811/2023 being filed and compromised.
Accordingly he denies other suggestions.
In the cross examination this witness admits she had full of love and affection did married accused No.1 at the time of marriage and she has compromised without any force or coercion.

10. On going through the material on record, as the complainant herself had turned hostile and submits she wants to compromise with the accused persons other than the offence punishable u/s.506 of IPC all other offences are compoundable.

On going through the citation of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in 2023 (4) KCCR 3544 in case of Tammanna V/s. State of Karnataka wherein the Hon'ble High Court has observed " the abusive words are be as such that it should be provocative so as to commit breach of public peace".

In the case on hand as observed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Part-A of Head Note :
Kodigehalli Ps vs A1 Venugopal Singh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169624525/
4 "A. Penal Code, 1860-Section 504-Evidence Act, 1872-Section 3-Acquittal-Insult with intent to provoke breach of public peace, not spoken to by witnesses in a consistent manner-mentioning of alleged abusive words in complaint and evidence of complainant alone cannot be basis for conviction of accused -Hence, acquitted."
There are no material to prove the alleged offence is my firm view.

sentences.text:
In the case on hand, to prove the ingredient of offence punishable u/s.506 of IPC the accused persons intimidated the complainant,
the material placed by the complainant are not sufficient to consider the same and the question of giving life threat is not satisfied in the evidence of the complainant and this fact is not corroborated in the evidence of P.W.1.
As the official witnesses are not examined, these Point Nos.1 to 4 are answered in the Negative.
11. POINT NO.5:

With regard to the offence punishable u/s.4 of D.P.Act, though the complaint has been made by the complainant and in the charge sheet the parents of the complainant are being made as witnesses, when the complainant herself has turned hostile and does not supports the prosecution case, there is no any material collected by the Investigating Officer concerning the amount taken by the accused from the complainant, with regard to the document No.3 pledging of the golden ornaments and amount being collected by the Investigating Officer, the copies of the documents have been placed which are not substantial piece of evidence.
Even in the cross examination complainant has not supported with regard to the accused No.1 had obtained any loan on her golden ornaments.
In fact the Investigating Officer has placed Ncr.No.556/2015 being registered on the basis of the complaint made by the complainant as on 12.12.2015.

Even during the course of investigation, the banker with whom the accused has pledged the golden ornaments of the complainant has not been made as witness whether the banker has been examined by the Investigating Officer is not forthcoming from the material on record.

Under these circumstances,
considering the hostility of the complainant, this court is satisfied not to examine other official witnesses since the caste of the parties is not disputed.
As such CWs.15 and 16 are being given up.
The C.W.14 has registered the marriage of the accused No.1 and the complainant which is undisputed, as such C.W.14 is not examined.
The C.W.11 is the Engineer of the BBMP who had visited the spot and conducted the spot sketch.
In fact the drawing of spot Mahazar itself has been contradicted by the complainant in her evidence.

Under these circumstances, to consider any incident happened as per the prosecution case, being not established and the hostility of the complainant is fatal to the prosecution case to bring home the guilt of the accused with regard to the offence punishable u/s.4 of the D.P.Act is my firm view.
Accordingly this Point No.5 is answered in the Negative.

12. POINT NO.6 to 8: In proof of ingredients of alleged offence punishable u/s.3(1)(r),(s) and (z) of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989 the complainant has specifically mentioned he has compounded the alleged offence against the accused Nos.1 and 2.
In fact complainant has specified in the complaint she has been abused by taking her caste.

The complainant belonging to the caste of 'Adi Karnataka' is not disputed, however with regard to abusive words used the complainant has not specified what are the words used by the accused persons while abusing the complainant.
The complainant in her examination-in-chief has specified accused No.1 and 2 abused her and what are the actual words used to abuse the complainant has not been specified even by the complainant.

Kodigehalli Ps vs A1 Venugopal Singh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169624525/
5 13.

sentences.text: To prove the ingredient of offence punishable u/s.3(1)(s) of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989, intimidation made by the accused has not been specified even in the evidence of complainant.
Moreover in the absence of corroboration to that effect, this court finds no any ingredients for the alleged offence being proved.

Further more the investigation is conducted by drawing spot Mahazar by the PSI who is not an authorised person as per the provisions of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989 and Rule 9 of SC/ST (POA)Rules 1985.
14.

To prove the ingredient of offence punishable u/s.3(1)(z) of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989, accused told the complainant to leave the house and assaulted her in a place within public view has not been specified even in the evidence of complainant.
Moreover in the absence of corroboration to that effect, this court finds no any ingredients for the alleged offence being proved.
Further more the investigation is conducted by drawing spot Mahazar by the PSI who is not an authorised person as per the provisions of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989 and Rule 9 of SC/ST (POA)Rules 1985.
Under these circumstances, this court is satisfied to answer these Points No.6 to 8 in the Negative.
15. POINT No.9 : The accused persons did complied the provisions of section 437A of Cr.P.C., by providing personal bond before this court, for their appearance before the Hon'ble Appellant court.
The accused No.1 and 2 are set at liberty.

However, the bond executed in compliance of Sec.437(A)
of Cr.P.C., shall be in force till appeal period.
(Dictated to the stenographer Grade I in open court, transcription thereof corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in open Court on this the 15 th day of May, 2024).
(Rajesh Karnam K) LXX Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge & Special Judge, Bangalore.
